column1: # The index set of CRISPRme 2.10.0 (the rebuild manifest): every archive the rebuild for 2.10.0
# builds and publishes in lucapinello/crisprme-indexes-format2 (decision C2), one per line, with
# how it is built and published. Read by seq_script/rebuild/check_index_set.py (the D7 readiness
# audit's check of the set against the code), the rebuild, and crisprme_hf.successor_index (which
# index of 2.10.0 a download of an archive of 2.8.1 names). seq_script/rebuild/README.md says how.
# Columns: archive (indexes/<archive>.tar.gz; build-inputs/<dataset> for an enriched-genome kit),
# kind (reference, variant, bundle, genotypes, indel-genotypes, build-inputs), panel (the variant
# dataset; - for the reference), pam_file, pam, side, spacer (guide length, nt), bmax (N, the index
# name's), bdna and brna (the build's --bDNA and --bRNA: N = max + 1), repo, replaces (the archives
# of 2.8.1 it replaces, comma-separated), build and publish (one bash command each, run from the
# repository's root, each on its own: a cd is inside ( ), so no command moves the next; a recipe
# is called by its repository path; a build first copies its PAM file from the repository's PAMs/
# into its working directory's; - for a panel companion, which the panel's first build writes and
# its first publish-index uploads), notes (- for none). The commands' variables
# (check_index_set.VARIABLES): $REF, $HGDP, $HPRC, $MEGA, one working directory per panel, each
# holding hg38 in Genomes/hg38, every index of a panel built in it, so that they share its one
# Dictionaries bundle; $RUN, the prefix that runs a command in the release image (empty where the
# release is installed); $SIF, that image, which the HGDP + 1000 Genomes and HPRC recipes run;
